daemon.noResponse: Aide’s background service isn’t responding. It usually starts automatically; if this continues, reopen Aide.

personal.connectMessage:
Please connect yourself to my computer (Aide):
1. Install: curl -fsSL https://github.com/samir2015dzh/aide/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh -s -- --cli
2. Log in: AIDE_PASSWORD='{{password}}' ~/.local/bin/aide auth login {{server}} --account {{account}} --name "{{name}}"
Then you’re ready. Use aide project list to see the projects you can use, aide session start --project {{project}} --prompt "…" to start working, and aide --help for every command.

health.processesBody: Process limit reached ({{used}} / {{limit}}). Aide can’t start coding agents, so new tasks will fail. It will recover automatically once the program holding those processes quits.
health.processesBodyCulprit: Process limit reached ({{used}} / {{limit}}), including {{count}} finished processes that {{culprit}} never cleaned up. Aide can’t start coding agents, so new tasks will fail. Quit {{culprit}} to recover automatically.
health.processesBodyNear: Processes are near the system limit ({{used}} / {{limit}}). Once reached, Aide won’t be able to start coding agents.
health.processesBodyNearCulprit: Processes are near the system limit ({{used}} / {{limit}}), including {{count}} finished processes that {{culprit}} never cleaned up. Quit {{culprit}} before Aide can no longer start coding agents.
health.diskBody: Only {{free}} remaining. When the disk is full, new tasks can’t create a worktree or save task records.
health.filesTitle: Aide on {{name}} is running out of open files
health.filesBody: {{used}} of {{limit}} open files in use. Restarting Aide helps; if this keeps happening, copy the diagnostics and send them to us.

health.shellPathBody: {{detail}}. Coding agents installed via nvm, npm, or similar tools may not be found. Check whether a new Terminal window opens slowly or waits for input. Aide retries every minute.

claude.title: Claude sessions
claude.note: The Claude Code sessions the Claude app has on your machines (not those Aide started). Read only.
claude.none: The Claude app lists no Claude Code sessions on your machines.

dsh.title: DeepSeek sessions
dsh.note: Sessions on your machines that DeepSeek Harness has of its own (opened in DSH, or by another tool). Read only, until you turn on Take Over for one: then you can send it messages from here.
dsh.none: No DeepSeek Harness sessions of its own on your machines.
dsh.localOff: This computer is not turned on as a machine, so its sessions don’t show here. Once on, you can turn it off again in Settings › Machines.
dsh.pick: Choose a session to read it.
dsh.unreachableLastKnown: {{name}} is lost: its sessions below are as last read.
dsh.lostNote: {{name}} can't be reached: what is shown is as last read. Its conversation can be read once it is back.
dsh.homeHint: If DSH Desktop has sessions that are not here, it keeps them in another folder: set the user environment variable DSH_HOME to that folder, and Aide reads there.
dsh.takeoverNote1: You can send this session messages and stop its turn from Aide. They go to DSH through the Aide plugin in DSH Desktop and show there too.
dsh.takeoverNote2: While a turn runs, a message waits for the next turn, as one typed in DSH would.
dsh.takeoverNote3: If you work on this session in Aide and DSH Desktop at once, messages queue in the order they arrive. Turning it off makes it read only again; the session in DSH is unaffected.
dsh.placeholder: Message this session… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
dsh.placeholderRunning: A turn is running: this waits for the next turn… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
dsh.queued: Queued: DSH takes it up when this turn ends.
dsh.notRunningHere: No turn of this session runs in DSH Desktop.

bridge.notInstalled: DSH Desktop doesn't have the Aide plugin yet, so messages can't go.
bridge.notRunning: The Aide plugin in DSH Desktop doesn't answer, so messages can't go.
bridge.incompatible: The Aide plugin in DSH Desktop can't be used.
bridge.unknown: Not known yet whether the Aide plugin in DSH Desktop runs.
